generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, this means bringing all three together whenever you work with others, whether it is a seminar presentation or a group lab report. You present your own analysis with authority and defend it when a peer questions your method, you listen to the rest of the group and build on their points, and you steer any disagreement about the design. Afterwards you reflect on how you worked together and carry one change into the next piece. Treating these as one practice is what makes you a psychology student others want on their team.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students work on the same group presentation about a memory study. Tom prepares his slides but goes quiet when the group argues over the method, and later writes only that 'the group worked well'. Amara presents her section with authority, answers a challenge about her sampling, listens to a teammate's worry about the design and folds it in, then reflects that stepping into the argument early is what held the team together. Both understood the study, but Amara brought authority, collaboration and reflection together on the one task.
generatedProse.summary: Presenting and working with others in psychology are most useful as one practice, not three separate skills. On every seminar talk and group report you bring authority, collaboration and reflection together, and carry one change into the next. It is this habit that makes you a psychologist who communicates clearly and works well in a team.

check.body: In a group presentation, a student owns their section and defends it, listens and adapts with the team, helps steer a disagreement, then reflects honestly afterwards. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the student is using presenting, collaborating and reflecting as one practice of working with people.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three are there, working together on the same piece of work.

_items.text: That the student is doing more than any one piece of group work really needs.
_items.feedback: No. Each part does a different job, and together they make the work stronger.

_items.text: That only the reflection at the end really mattered.
_items.feedback: Not so. The authority and collaboration did the real work, and reflection improves the next round.

_items.text: That presenting and collaborating are the same thing.
_items.feedback: They are different parts of the one practice, used together rather than merged.
